grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, sprouts, onion, garlic, tinned chickpeas, olive oil, thyme and smoked paprika are all plain whole foods or ordinary cupboard staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket, and sprouts are cheap and plentiful in December.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, a frying pan and a colander, and the techniques are parboiling and frying.

works.reason: Parboiling the diced potatoes for 6 minutes then frying gives a sensible crisp hash, and the quantities suit four. The pan will be full by the time the sprouts and chickpeas go in, but a cook would manage.

honest_times.reason: About 10 minutes of peeling and chopping plus about 21 minutes of stirring at the frying pan fits the 30 minutes prep. Bringing the water up and the 6-minute boil roughly matches the 10 minutes cook.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the thyme and smoked paprika, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot potato and sprout hash suits a cold morning just before Christmas, and the potatoes are clearly the base of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Potatoes, sprouts and chickpeas make a filling breakfast with vegetables and pulses that a family would happily eat again.
